senses.definition: An animal from a group that included animals such as Triceratops and includes birds today. All dinosaurs outside the bird group died out long ago.
senses.example: The museum had a tall model of a dinosaur with three horns.

senses.definition: To put something into a liquid briefly, or move down and back up.
senses.example: I dipped the paintbrush into the water.

senses.definition: A place that slopes down and rises again.
senses.example: The trail crossed a dip between the two hills.

senses.definition: A sauce or soft food that you put another food into before eating it.
senses.example: We ate carrots with a yogurt dip.

senses.definition: Going straight to a place or point without a stop or change.
senses.example: We took a direct path from the playground to school.

senses.definition: Clear and open about what you mean.
senses.example: She gave me a direct answer to the question.

senses.definition: To guide, aim, or be in charge of something.
senses.example: Our teacher directed the school play.

senses.definition: The way in which someone or something moves, points, or faces.
senses.example: The arrow shows the direction of the exit.

senses.definition: An instruction that tells where to go or what to do.
senses.example: Please read each direction before starting the game.

senses.definition: Loose earth or other material on the ground, or a substance that makes something unclean.
senses.example: My boots left dirt on the porch.

senses.definition: A condition that makes some activities or tasks harder for a person, especially when a place or activity is not designed for their needs.
senses.example: Having a disability does not make everyone need the same kind of help.

senses.definition: To have a different idea or opinion from someone else.
senses.example: We disagree about the best way to build the tower.

senses.definition: To go out of sight or stop being present.
senses.example: The rabbit disappeared into the bushes.

senses.definition: To seem to vanish completely, leaving no clue where something went.
senses.example: My left sock seemed to disappear into thin air.

senses.definition: To make someone feel sad because things did not go as hoped.
senses.example: The change in plans may disappoint the players.

senses.definition: A very bad event that causes much damage or hardship.
senses.example: The town planted trees again after the flood disaster.

senses.definition: A complete failure, often used to describe something less serious.
senses.example: The cake was a disaster because I forgot to put in the flour.

senses.definition: To find or learn something you did not know before.
senses.example: We discovered a second path down to the pond.

senses.definition: To talk about a subject and share ideas or information.
senses.example: The group will discuss the first chapter tomorrow.

senses.definition: Clothes or changes that make someone or something hard to recognize.
senses.example: A wig and hat were part of her disguise.

senses.definition: To change the way someone or something looks so people do not recognize it.
senses.example: The dancer disguised the tall stool as a tree trunk.

senses.definition: To show something clearly so that others can see it.
senses.example: The class displayed its artwork in the hall.

senses.definition: Things set out for people to look at.
senses.example: There was a display of model boats in the window.

senses.definition: A screen or set of lights that shows information.
senses.example: The display on the clock showed the wrong time.

senses.definition: To spread through another material in particles so small that you no longer see the separate pieces.
senses.example: The sugar began to dissolve in the water.

senses.definition: Oxygen gas mixed into water in a form many water animals can use to breathe.
senses.example: The trout took dissolved oxygen from the water through its gills.

senses.definition: How far it is from one point to another.
senses.example: We measured the distance from the door to the gate.

senses.definition: Clearly different or separate.
senses.example: I heard two distinct knocks.

senses.definition: Easy to notice, hear, or see.
senses.example: There was a distinct smell of lemon in the room.

senses.definition: To turn someone’s attention away from what they were doing.
senses.example: The funny noises distracted me from my reading.

senses.definition: A place that gathers products before sending the right amounts on to different destinations.
senses.example: The distribution center sent one load to three small shops.

senses.definition: A rule that lets you multiply the parts of a sum or difference separately, then put the results back together.
senses.example: By the distributive property, four times 12 equals four times ten plus four times two.

senses.definition: To separate something into parts or groups.
senses.example: Divide the crayons between the two tables.

senses.definition: In math, to find the size of equal groups or how many times one number fits into another.
senses.example: If you divide twelve by three, you get four.

senses.definition: Feeling as though you or things around you are spinning, or feeling unsteady.
senses.example: The quick ride made me dizzy for a minute.

senses.definition: The long material carrying inherited information that many cells keep and use.
senses.example: The cell holds much of its DNA in a nucleus.

senses.definition: To act, work on a task, or carry it out.
senses.example: I will do the dishes after the game.

senses.definition: A word used before another action word to make some questions, negatives, or strong statements.
senses.example: Do you like puzzles? I do like them!

senses.definition: A platform or part of a harbor where boats stop.
senses.example: We tied the boat at a wooden dock.

senses.definition: To bring a ship or other vehicle to a place where it can stop or join another vehicle.
senses.example: The ferry will dock at the island at noon.

senses.definition: To move aside quickly to avoid being hit or to avoid dealing with something directly.
senses.example: I stepped to one side to dodge the bouncing ball.

senses.definition: A unit of money used in the United States and some other countries.
senses.example: I saved one dollar for a postcard.

senses.definition: A mammal that usually lives in the sea, has a smooth body and flippers, and comes to the surface to breathe.
senses.example: A dolphin rose from the water near the ferry.

senses.definition: A readable name used to identify a place or group of places on a network.
senses.example: Two pages on the site can share a domain name.

senses.definition: A round roof or ceiling that curves upward like part of a ball.
senses.example: Sunlight streamed in through windows under the dome.

senses.definition: A small playing tile usually marked into two halves, each with a number of dots.
senses.example: I matched a domino with five dots at the end of the row.

senses.definition: To give money, objects, or time to help other people or a cause.
senses.example: We donated our outgrown coats to a winter clothing drive.

senses.definition: An animal related to horses, usually with large ears and a gray or brown coat.
senses.example: A donkey carried bags along the trail.

senses.definition: To make a small, casual drawing, often while thinking about something else.
senses.example: We doodled stars and squares on our scrap paper.

senses.definition: A small, casual drawing.
senses.example: A doodle of a snail filled the bottom corner of the page.

senses.definition: A round handle you often turn to open or close a door.
senses.example: I turned the doorknob and stepped into the room.

senses.definition: Not active or growing now, but able to become active later.
senses.example: The plant stayed dormant through the winter.

senses.definition: A fin that rises from the back of a swimming animal.
senses.example: The orca’s dorsal fin showed above the water.

senses.definition: A graph that shows data by placing dots over the matching marks on a number line.
senses.example: Our dot plot had two dots over nine because two leaves were that length.

senses.definition: Twice as much or made with two parts.
senses.example: We need a double batch of muffins today.

senses.definition: To make or become twice as much.
senses.example: We will double the time from five minutes to ten.

senses.definition: A person who looks very much like another person, or who takes an actor’s place in a scene.
senses.example: A stunt double climbed the wall for the actor.

senses.definition: A window with two sheets of glass and a sealed space between them.
senses.example: A double-pane window helped slow the movement of heat out of the room.

senses.definition: A feeling of being unsure that something is true or will happen.
senses.example: I had some doubt about whether the gate would be open.

senses.definition: To feel unsure or think something may not be true.
senses.example: I doubt that the little box can hold a bowling ball.

senses.definition: A bird related to a pigeon, often with a round body and a soft call.
senses.example: A dove called from the tree outside our window.

senses.definition: A past form of dive.
senses.example: The swimmer dove into the pool.

senses.definition: A short or sudden period of very heavy rain.
senses.example: A downpour soaked the picnic blanket in a few minutes.

senses.definition: The main area of a city or town where many businesses are close together.
senses.example: Our town’s downtown has a library and several small shops.

senses.definition: Toward or in the main business area of a town or city.
senses.example: We rode downtown to pick up a new library card.

senses.definition: To sleep lightly, usually for a short time.
senses.example: I dozed on the bus after our long field trip.

senses.definition: A group of twelve.
senses.example: Dad bought a dozen eggs at the store.

senses.definition: A first or unfinished version of a written work, drawing, or plan.
senses.example: My first draft still has a blank space for the ending.

senses.definition: A current of air moving through a space, especially indoors.
senses.example: A draft came in under the door.

senses.definition: To write or draw a first version of something.
senses.example: I drafted a note to thank the volunteers.

senses.definition: A force from a fluid such as air or water that opposes movement through it.
senses.example: Drag made it harder to ride my bike into the wind.

senses.definition: An opening or pipe that carries water away.
senses.example: The drain at the bottom of the sink caught a grape.

senses.definition: To let water or another liquid flow out.
senses.example: We drained the extra water from the pan.

senses.definition: To use up energy or another supply little by little.
senses.example: Running the game all afternoon drained the battery.

senses.definition: A curved part of a drain that holds water to block air and smells from farther down the pipe.
senses.example: A drain trap under the sink held a small amount of water.

senses.definition: All the land where water runs toward the same river, lake or other low place.
senses.example: The streams in the same drainage basin eventually reached one river.

senses.definition: A line of high ground that separates areas where water flows toward different streams, lakes, or other places.
senses.example: Rain ran toward different creeks on the two sides of the drainage divide.

senses.definition: A story written to be acted, or a type of story with serious events.
senses.example: The class watched a short drama about a missing letter.

senses.definition: A situation with strong feelings or surprises.
senses.example: There was drama when the little dog escaped just before the show.

senses.definition: Strong or extreme in a way that causes a big change.
senses.example: We made a drastic change by switching from one large race to several small ones.

senses.definition: To make a picture, shape, or line by marking a surface.
senses.example: Let’s draw a map of the park.

senses.definition: To pull something in a direction or get something from a place.
senses.example: I will draw a name from the hat.

senses.definition: A game or contest that ends without a winner.
senses.example: Neither team scored, so the match ended in a draw.

senses.definition: To be unable to remember or think of the thing you are looking for.
senses.example: I knew the dog’s name yesterday, but today I draw a blank every time.

senses.definition: A bridge with a part that can be lifted or moved so boats can pass or so an entrance can be closed.
senses.example: The drawbridge rose before the tall boat went through.

senses.definition: A container that slides in and out of a piece of furniture.
senses.example: The extra pencils are in the top drawer.

senses.definition: Images and events your mind makes while you sleep.
senses.example: I had a dream about a talking bike.

senses.definition: Something you strongly hope will happen.
senses.example: Her dream is to play the violin in a concert.

senses.definition: To have a dream or imagine something you want.
senses.example: My brother dreams of visiting a desert.

senses.definition: To control a ball while moving, such as by bouncing it in basketball or with small kicks in soccer.
senses.example: Maya learned to dribble a basketball with either hand.

senses.definition: To let a liquid run in a thin trickle or a few little drops.
senses.example: The rain began to dribble down the window.

senses.definition: To move slowly without much control or effort.
senses.example: We watched leaves drift across the pond.

senses.definition: A pile of snow, sand, or other material gathered by wind or water.
senses.example: A drift of snow blocked the back door.

senses.definition: To take a liquid into your mouth and swallow it.
senses.example: I stopped to drink some water after the race.

senses.definition: A liquid that people can swallow, such as water, milk, or juice.
senses.example: Water is my favorite drink when I am thirsty.

senses.definition: To fall in drops or let liquid fall in drops.
senses.example: Water dripped from the edge of the roof.

senses.definition: A falling drop, or the continuing sound or action of drops falling.
senses.example: We could hear a slow drip in the sink.

senses.definition: To control the movement of a car, truck, or other vehicle.
senses.example: My aunt will drive us to the museum.

senses.definition: A trip in a vehicle.
senses.example: We took a drive through the hills.

senses.definition: Light rain made up of very small drops.
senses.example: A drizzle left tiny drops on our glasses.

senses.definition: To rain lightly or pour a thin stream of liquid over something.
senses.example: I drizzled a little honey over the fruit.

senses.definition: A small amount of liquid that hangs or falls as one bit.
senses.example: A drop of water fell onto my sleeve.

senses.definition: A fall or decrease in amount, level, or position.
senses.example: By morning, we noticed a drop in temperature.

senses.definition: To let something fall, or to become lower.
senses.example: Please don’t drop the jar.

senses.definition: To take someone or something to a place and leave them or it there.
senses.example: Could we drop off my library books before soccer?

senses.definition: To fall asleep, often slowly or without meaning to.
senses.example: I started to drop off while my brother read the last page.

senses.definition: To become smaller in number, amount, or strength.
senses.example: The number of birds at the feeder began to drop off when the storm passed.

senses.definition: A long period when a place has less water than usual, often because too little rain or snow falls.
senses.example: The pond nearly dried up during the drought.

senses.definition: A planned contest between two people, historically sometimes a fight.
senses.example: Two players faced each other in a friendly spelling duel.

senses.definition: To compete directly against one other person.
senses.example: The two finalists dueled in a close game of chess.

senses.definition: A piece of music meant for two people to perform together, or its performance.
senses.example: My brother and I practiced our piano duet.

senses.definition: Not sharp at an edge or point.
senses.example: These dull scissors will not cut the cloth.

senses.definition: Not bright, clear, or interesting.
senses.example: The sky was a dull gray all afternoon.

senses.definition: To make or become less sharp, strong, or bright.
senses.example: Dust can dull the shine of a mirror.

senses.definition: A hill or ridge of sand pushed together by wind or water.
senses.example: Beach grass helped keep sand from blowing away from the dune.

senses.definition: At some time within an event or period of time.
senses.example: A dog barked during our music lesson.

senses.definition: Something you are expected or required to do.
senses.example: One of my duties is feeding the cat in the morning.

senses.definition: An object that orbits the Sun, is nearly round, and shares its neighborhood with other objects of similar importance. It is not a moon.
senses.example: Pluto and Ceres are both dwarf planets.

senses.definition: To live in a place.
senses.example: The family dwelt in a small stone house.

senses.definition: To spend a long time thinking or talking about something, often followed by “on.”
senses.example: We decided not to dwell on the missed basket and kept playing.

senses.definition: A substance that adds color to cloth, hair, or another material.
senses.example: We used blue dye to color the ribbon.

senses.definition: To use a substance to change the color of a material.
senses.example: Will you dye the cloth before or after sewing it?

senses.definition: A microphone that uses a moving coil of wire or thin metal ribbon near a magnet to turn sound into an electrical signal.
senses.example: We spoke into a dynamic microphone to record the announcement.

senses.definition: How loud or soft sounds are in music and how the loudness changes.
senses.example: The conductor asked the group to watch the dynamics in the last part.

senses.definition: A line of rulers from the same family, or the stretch of time when that family rules.
senses.example: The Tang dynasty ruled China for almost three hundred years.
